claims.claim: Athenagoras was an Athenian philosopher who converted to Christianity and wrote as a Christian apologist in the second half of the second century.
The work was written to answer the doubts of pagan philosophers and other critics who claimed that bodily resurrection was impossible or contrary to God’s will.

In its introduction Athenagoras explicitly addresses “those who disbelieve or doubt concerning the resurrection,” urging them to examine the issue rationally rather than on the basis of idle speculation.

The treatise forms part of Athenagoras’s broader apologetic effort, which also included an “Embassy for the Christians” addressed to Emperor Marcus Aurelius and his son Commodus to refute accusations of atheism, cannibalism, and incest against Christians.

The text survives in a number of Greek manuscripts; seventeen medieval copies are known, and it has been printed in modern editions beginning with Henry Stephens’s 1557 edition, often together with the Apology.
